title: Perfect tests suffice for bounded-above tensor finiteness
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over $A$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ satisfy $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all $i>b$ for some integer $b$ [def-pc-derived-category]. If $R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_X}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every perfect $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex, def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], then $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_X}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every pseudo-coherent $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex].

proof.text: Apply the uniform inverse-affine-sections bound to the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. This morphism is qcqs by the hypothesis that $X$ is a qcqs scheme. Obtain $N>0$ with $R^p\Gamma(X,M)=0$ for every quasi-coherent module $M$ and every $p\ge N$. Global sections commute with countable products: a section of a product sheaf is exactly a tuple of sections. The unbounded-derived-functor bound therefore gives $H^i(R\Gamma(X,L))=0$ for $i>t+N-1$ whenever $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ has no cohomology above $t$. This bound also holds for the $A$-module-valued sections in the statement: on a K-injective representative both versions have the same underlying complex of abelian groups, and a module is zero when its underlying group is zero.

source.place: Tag 0CSH, lemma-perfect-enough, proof first paragraph; Tags 08D5 and 08D4(3)

proof.text: Fix a pseudo-coherent $E$ and an arbitrary integer $m$. Put $a=m-N-1-b$. Apply perfect approximation to obtain $u:P\to E$ which is an isomorphism on $H^i$ for $i>a$ and a surjection for $i=a$. Complete $u$ to a distinguished triangle $P\to E\to C\to P[1]$. Here $P$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by the approximation statement, $E$ does by pseudo-coherence, and $C$ does by the triangulated quasi-coherent-subcategory lemma, applied with $T=X$ to the rotation $E\to C\to P[1]\to E[1]$.

source.place: Tag 0CSH, proof: perfect approximation and cone triangle; Tag 08ES

proof.text: The cohomology exact sequence of this cone triangle gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\ge a$: in $H^i(P)\to H^i(E)\to H^i(C)\to H^{i+1}(P)\to H^{i+1}(E)$ the first map is surjective and the last injective. This is the usual cohomological-functor exact sequence (on cone representatives it is the sequence of $0\to E^\bullet\to C(u)^\bullet\to P^\bullet[1]\to0$).

source.place: Tag 0CSH, proof: cone has zero cohomology in degrees at least m-N-1-b

proof.text: Use the standard truncation description to represent $C$ by a complex zero above $a-1$ and $K$ by one zero above $b$. The bounded-above flat-replacement lemma gives quasi-isomorphic flat complexes with those same upper term bounds; they are K-flat by the bounded-above-flat lemma. Their total tensor computes $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$. In degree $j>a-1+b$ each summand $F^r\otimes G^s$, $r+s=j$, is zero, since $r\le a-1$ and $s\le b$ cannot both hold. Hence $H^j(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)=0$ for $j\ge a+b=m-N-1$. This is a direct degree calculation from the cited replacement statements, not an additional approximation lemma.

source.place: Tag 0CSH, proof: tensor-cone upper bound; cohomology.tex Tag 06YD; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YS

proof.text: Both $C$ and $K$ have quasi-coherent cohomology, so the canonical tensor quasi-coherence lemma applies to $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$. The bound of step 1 with $t=m-N-2$ shows that $R\Gamma(X,C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ has zero cohomology for $i>m-3$, in particular for every $i\ge m-1$. No flatness of $K$ or boundedness below of either factor is used.

source.place: Tag 0CSH, proof: derived sections of the tensor cone; Tags 08DX and 08D4(3)

proof.text: Tensor the triangle of step 2 with $K$ and apply $R\Gamma(X,-)$. Tensoring is exact by the fixed-K-flat-tensor triangulated lemma: choose a flat-term K-flat representative of $K$ using the site-derived-tensor descent equivalence. The right-derived-functor triangulated lemma applies to global sections, giving a distinguished triangle with vertices $T_P=R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$, $T_E=R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ and $T_C=R\Gamma(X,C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ in $D(A)$. In its cohomology sequence, $H^{i-1}(T_C)=H^i(T_C)=0$ for $i\ge m$ by step 5. Thus $H^i(T_P)\to H^i(T_E)$ is an isomorphism for all $i\ge m$.

source.place: Tag 0CSH, proof: RΓ(P tensor K) to RΓ(E tensor K) isomorphism in high degrees; cohomology.tex Tag 06Y8

proof.text: By the hypothesis on perfect tests, $T_P$ is pseudo-coherent. Hence it is $m$-pseudo-coherent by the ring criterion: choose a bounded finite-free complex $F$ and $F\to T_P$ inducing cohomology isomorphisms for $i>m$ and a surjection for $i=m$. Compose with $T_P\to T_E$. Step 6 makes the composite an isomorphism for $i>m$ and surjective for $i=m$, so the definition says that $T_E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Since $m$ was arbitrary, the same ring criterion implies that $T_E$ is pseudo-coherent. This applies to every pseudo-coherent $E$, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q58-5690f59ef (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and every cited statement in full. Sources checked: Stacks perfect.tex 0CSH lemma-perfect-enough (l.8648, statement and proof) and 08EM/08EN/08ES. The item's statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live, which still has the item unsplit, and they match 0CSH: K in D^-_QCoh, A arbitrary, X qcqs. New node lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-perfect-approximation is 08ES with T=X. The empty support condition is harmless, the loss r is absorbed because E is pseudo-coherent, and E is in D_QCoh by lem-sc-pseudo-coherent-qcoh. It is statement-only, self-contained, cites its definitions and has correct source labels. Small cases: X empty; E=0; affine X over a non-Noetherian ring via the stupid truncation of a finite-free resolution (iso on H^i for i>a, ker d^a onto H^a at a); E unbounded below. Duplicate search: rg -L for 08ES/08EN/08EM/0CSH and for perfect+approximat over the snapshot DAG, plus the blueprint main-20261015, found nothing. Steps: (1) the uniform bound via X->Spec Z gives N, and the unbounded-functor lemma gives vanishing for i>t+N-1; (2) a=m-N-1-b, and C is QCoh by the triangulated lemma applied to the rotation; (3) H^i(C)=0 for i>=a, endpoint included; (4) flat replacements keep their upper bounds, so the tensor vanishes in degrees >=a+b=m-N-1; (5) t=m-N-2 gives vanishing for i>m-3; (6) the fixed-K-flat tensor and RGamma are exact, and H^{i-1}(T_C)=H^i(T_C)=0 for i>=m gives isomorphisms for i>=m; (7) composing with the finite-free m-approximation of T_P makes T_E m-pseudo-coherent for every m. The arithmetic matches Stacks, and nothing from the source proof was dropped. I accept the 12 generic off-unit tool_uses. No SGA source is cited. No fixes.
